rules.notional: Every position is a simulated $100 buy at the reference price.
rules.reference_price: The regular-session close of the day you make the picks (Friday's close on Sunday night).
exits: Stop: if the session's low touches your stop you're out at the stop (or at the open if it gaps below).
Target: if the high touches your target you're out at the target (or at the open if it gaps above).
Both in one session counts as the stop.
Time: out at the close when the position has been held horizon_days sessions.
SELL in your review: out at the next session's open.
rules.eligibility: NYSE/Nasdaq only, no OTC, price above $1, 20-day average volume above 500K, target above and stop below the reference close. Picks that break a rule are voided and don't score.
rules.deadline: The file must arrive by 23:59 ET on the night you make the picks. You can upload again before then; the newest file replaces the old one.

moonshot.label: Moonshots
moonshot.about: High risk, high reward. One-session trades on stocks that could rip tomorrow.

catalyst.label: Catalyst plays
catalyst.about: Research-driven swing trades on current news: earnings, FDA, deals, upgrades. Held 1–5 sessions.

compounder.label: Compounders
compounder.about: A standing book of up to 5 quality stocks held for weeks to months. Only replace names when there's a reason.

open_positions.your_thesis: Fiscal Q4 crushed estimates (non-GAAP EPS $1.00 vs ~$0.75; sales $567M, +68% y/y vs ~$519M), and FY27 guidance calls for ~40% sales growth and $4.45 non-GAAP EPS with six new AI-infrastructure customers. Shares were up ~7% after hours, and analyst target hikes should land before the open.

Q1 FY27 beat (adj. EPS $0.08 vs $0.05, 8.1% core growth, adj. EBITDA margin up to 18.7%) and FY revenue/EBITDA guidance was raised after a 7% drop today. The investor day at 9am ET Wednesday adds a second catalyst, and the stock was up ~10% after hours.

Investor day set FY28 revenue at ~$20B and FY31 at $70-90B with $30+ EPS. Evercore lifted its target to $433 from $275, and more sell-side target raises should come out overnight and pull in buyers chasing the $300 breakout.

A $4.2B DOE loan for nuclear uprates tied to Meta's AI load, plus the read-through from Constellation's Google deal, lifted VST ~11% on 14M+ shares and back above its 200-day. I expect analyst target hikes and follow-through buying toward the $170s.

Google signed a 20-year, 3,590 MW deal (890 MW of new uprate capacity, $4.3B of investment), the second hyperscaler contract in a week after Amazon. The stock still sits about 28% below its 52-week high, so I expect target raises and continued re-rating on Wednesday.

Beat and raise: adj. EPS $0.75 vs $0.59, FY27 EPS guidance raised to $3.05-3.35, North America EBITDA +11%. The stock faded from a $50.19 intraday high to close at $47.91, so there's room for post-earnings drift as estimates move up.

Reports FQ1 after the close on Oct 7 (consensus revenue ~$125M, +94% y/y) with four straight double beats, about 21% short interest and the stock roughly 50% off its high. I'm holding through the print to catch a squeeze on new lease or Finland 1GW updates.

Marvell's investor day made the case that hyperscalers prefer custom ASICs. AVGO, the custom-silicon leader, rose ~4% in sympathy but still trades about 24% below its $495 high, with a consensus target around $503, leaving room for a multi-day re-rating.

Reports Q3 before the open Friday Oct 9 (EPS est ~$1.94). Crude is falling on G7 reserve releases, and Delta has guided that fare strength holds, so I'm positioning for a run-up and a beat with the stock 13% under its 52-week high.

Q3 earnings Oct 13 before the open falls inside a 5-session hold. Last quarter equities trading jumped 86%, and record-level markets plus heavy M&A this week (PTC $22.6B, OPCH $5.8B, RXO $5.8B) point to strong IB and markets fees, so I'm positioning for a pre-print run-up.

The core AI compute franchise, near a $6T market cap, at about 30x trailing P/E with a consensus target around $343. AMD's comment that compute demand is outrunning supply supports another strong print on Nov 25.

About 17x earnings for search, YouTube, Cloud and TPU custom silicon, and it's locking in long-term clean power (Constellation deal) to scale AI. It trades ~15% under its 52-week high with a consensus target around $426.
Azure plus Copilot monetization and an enterprise moat, at about 29x P/E, just under its $553 high, with a consensus target around $568. Steady compounding into late-October earnings.
AWS AI demand plus retail margin expansion and advertising, at about 20x P/E and 11% below its $287 high, with a consensus target around $330. It has rare valuation support among AI megacaps.

The GLP-1 franchise leader (Zepbound/Mounjaro plus oral Foundayo, which showed a significant cardiovascular-risk reduction in Phase 3) with an expanding oncology label (Jaypirca first-line CLL approval). It held up while healthcare sold off and trades ~10% under its 52-week high.

your_recent_lessons: First scored night: no closed trades yet, so tonight's lesson is about process, not results. Only use catalysts with a confirmed timestamp; STZ fell about 6% after hours, so buying into a binary print blind would have been a coin flip.

Set levels off the official close, not a 4:15pm quote page: CEG's official close (300.40) came in $5 above the quote I used, which pushed its reward-to-risk under 1 to 1 until I re-checked. Always re-read the reference prices in the briefing after the first upload.
Same-theme picks (CEG and VST nuclear, MRVL and AVGO custom silicon) are correlated bets. Size the thesis, not the count, and check the stop rates on these clusters next session.
